newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 6.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* A Florida state court jury found RJ Reynolds Tobacco was not responsible for the death of a smoker who died of lung cancer, in a big win for the tobacco industry.
* The Dow Jones industrials closed up 143.29 points at 7,214.49 helped by the tobacco ruling and a U.S. budget deal.
* According to people familiar with the plans, Bell Atlantic and NYNEX could cut their combined 137,000 workforce by at least 10,000, more than three times their initial estimate.
* Police and stock regulators stepped up efforts to uncover who was responsible for the scandal surrounding Bre-X Minerals' admission its Busang field contained insignificant amounts of gold.
* Ford light vehicle sales declined 4.3 percent in April while Japanese car makers benefited from the firm dollar and popular models.
* The U.S. Food and Drug Administration decided not to clear generic versions of American Home Products' widely-sold estrogen replacement therapy drug Premarin.
* Northrop Grumman said it agreed to purchase Logicon Inc, which makes advanced defense electronics and training systems, in a stock swap valued at about $750 million.
* A Donaldson, Lufkin unit agreed to purchase 85 percent of DecisionOne for cash and stock valued at $690 million.
* America Online posted a return to profitability in the quarter.
* Incentive AB announced plans to buy Vivra for $1.59 billion, forming one of the world's biggest kidney care groups.
* GTE plans to buy Internet firm BBN, according to people close to the matter. An industry executive valued the deal at up to $1 billion.
* The board of Andersen Worldwide nominated accounting partner Jim Wadia as its next chief executive.
* Kodak is set to start a campaign to interest U.S. children aged five to 12 in photography.
* At the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting, investor guru Warren Buffett warned of "conditions that can lead to excess" in the stock market.
* Huntington Bancshares said it would buy First Michigan Bank in a stock deal valued around $897 million.

* Heard on the Street: Even as he tried to temper his recent cautions about the stock market's sky-high levels, legendary investor Warren Buffett once again sounded a dubious note about whether further market advances can be supported.
* Credit markets: Bonds edged higher yesterday, stretching their winning streak to six days.
